summary: Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. A graduate student under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox at the University of Washington (attested 1999), he also held posts there, attested in 1998 and as professor in 2017.

Timothy Lubin works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1994, taught Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a post at Washington and Lee University, attested in 2020.
Tina Rasmussen specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed an MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Mysore, The Queen's College, Oxford (1914), and under Ramamohana Brahmachari (~1915–1922), among others. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College.

Tissa Rajapatirana works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and later held an attested post there in South Asian and Buddhist Studies in 1988.
Tiziana Pontillo (born 1969) is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd Gibson works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University under György Kara, earning his PhD (attested 1991).

Todd T. Lewis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University with mentors including Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah and Alex Wayman, and held posts at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996, 2016–2017).

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He obtained a geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923) and held posts at Tohoku University (1925), the University of Tokyo (1924), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen studied under David Pingree in 2008 and under Kim Plofker.

Tokio Takata (born 1949) specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, later holding posts at Kyoto University (1983–2014) and Fudan University (2016–2022).
Tokiyuki Hojo (1858–1929) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). He held posts at Kanazawa University (~1894–1898), Yamaguchi University (~1898–1899), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held posts at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Normal School and Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held teaching posts at Fukui Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida, the University of Freiburg, and under Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi, Kyoto, and Ryukoku universities, and was president of Kyoto University of Education.

Tom Tillemans (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Jacques May, served as Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary (~2005), and was a long-time professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018).

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara (PhD ~1985). She held faculty posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999, ~2000).
Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. Attested in 2012, Oshima studied under Toshifumi Goto and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University.
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University and held a post there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Uno was a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).
